channel.title: Rest of World - Latest
channel.description: A continuous stream of the latest articles published from Rest of World

item.title: The catch in IBM’s offer to relocate its U.S.-based immigrant workers
item.dc:creator: Ananya Bhattacharya
item.description: Ending U.S. visa sponsorship and shifting roles abroad helps the company retain talent, but leaves employees paying a steep financial and personal price.

item.title: AI isn’t replacing your job. It’s turning it into low-paid gig work
item.dc:creator: Julián Posada
item.description: Platform companies are luring doctors, lawyers, and Ph.D.s with top rates, but then use the same tactics of pay cuts and sudden ghosting that have plagued global data workers.
item.media:description: Surgeon Kapil Sahnan uses a DaVinci Robot during surgery on a woman, 2026.

item.title: The small African lab sounding the alarm on AI bioweapons
item.dc:creator: Danai Nesta Kupemba
item.description: MinoHealth researchers in Ghana jailbroke their own LLM as a test. What emerged were thousands of toxin recipes—and an urgent push for regulation.
item.media:credit: Agbongua Kwadwo Buenortey for Rest of World
item.media:description: Photograph showing Georgina an AI Engineer building and working on the user interface of the new model Moremi.

item.title: How Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia impacts China’s AI supply chain
item.dc:creator: Rest of World Staff
item.description: The founder’s stunning departure removes Beijing’s biggest advocate in Silicon Valley, accelerates chip stockpiling, and leaves Asian suppliers bracing for what comes next.
item.media:description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attends a summit at the Institute of Peace on October 8, 2026 in Washington, DC.

item.title: The promise and peril of AI in government
item.dc:creator: Beth Simone Noveck
item.description: In her new book “Reboot: AI and the Race to Save Democracy,” writer Beth Simone Noveck warns that while AI can increase efficiency, predictive models pose significant ethical and societal risks.
